subject: Sender cover vs beneficiary-net instruction — bank chain visibility for BRL/EUR settlement
messages:
From: Teresa Moskowitz <teresa.moskowitz@astramed.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ap@astramed.com
Date: Tue, 7 Nov 2028 13:22:00 +0000
Subject: Payment for RDW-5421 — intermediary fees / bank chain question

Hi Olga / Marissa,

We're ready to send payment for invoice RDW-5421 (attached) but our bank flagged the beneficiary FX leg: we will pay EUR from our EUR account; the beneficiary (Redwood Brazil) expects BRL. The bank says there may be one or more intermediary banks between the EUR debit and the BRL credit and that those intermediaries may deduct fees.

Two quick questions so we can instruct treasury: 1) Do you accept "sender pays all intermediary fees" (OUR) style instructions so AstraMed covers any corr/bank fees end-to-end? 2) If not, can Redwood provide a recommended instruction that results in the beneficiary receiving the invoice amount in BRL (i.e., Redwood absorbs/covers any intermediary deductions) — and if Redwood absorbs, how do you want us to reflect that on the payment advice so your accounting can reconcile?

We need to confirm before EOD Friday to meet our payment run.

Thanks — Teresa
Teresa Moskowitz
Head of Accounts Payable
AstraMed Inc
ap@astramed.com

Attachments: invoice_RDW-5421-AstraMed.pdf

From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Teresa Moskowitz <teresa.moskowitz@astramed.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 8 Nov 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Payment for RDW-5421 — intermediary fees / bank chain question

Teresa — thanks for the clear note and the invoice. Short answers up front: we can accept either approach, but each has tradeoffs. Below are two practical, templated options and the reconciliation notes we need. I've attached a short "wire instruction templates" doc with sample text.

Option A — Sender pays all intermediary fees (recommended for predictable cashflows)
- Instruction for payer bank: Sender to select OUR charges. Payment should be sent to: Redwood Brasil Ltda — Bank: Banco XYZ BR — Account ending 4321 — SWIFT: XYZBBRSP.
- Benefit: AstraMed bears all unpredictable intermediary deductions; Redwood records the full invoice amount as received.
- Accounting: Please include an electronic SWIFT MT103/Payment Advice to ap@redwood.com and cc finance@redwood.com. If intermediaries charge additional fees, we will not invoice you for them.

Option B — Beneficiary net (Redwood absorbs intermediary deductions)
- Instruction: Payer sends payment SHA (shared) or BEN; beneficiary will receive the net after intermediaries.
- Redwood needs: (1) a copy of the payment instruction/payment advice showing the gross amount, (2) the final value received, and (3) any intermediary fee messages if included in the remittance.
- Accounting impact: Redwood will record the gross as revenue and book the intermediary fees as a separate bank/finance expense. For clarity in your reconciliation, please add a short remittance note: "Payment for invoice RDW-5421 — gross EUR 42,000 — beneficiary to receive BRL equivalent."

Tax/VAT note (important): If Redwood absorbs intermediary fees, those fees are recorded in our books as financial expense. They do not change the taxable base of the underlying supply for VAT purposes in BR. Laura (cc'd) — can you confirm if we should issue a separate reimbursable invoice line for intermediary fees or keep it as an internal cost?

Next steps: if AstraMed wants the OUR option, we can provide a short payment instruction text you can paste into your bank portal. If you prefer SHA/BEN, please send a payment advice after the payment posts so we can reconcile.

I'll leave final wording to Marissa for commercial alignment.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Sr. Finance Ops (Commercial)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: wire_instruction_templates.docx, redwood_br_account_stub.pdf

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Teresa Moskowitz <teresa.moskowitz@astramed.com>
Cc: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 9 Nov 2028 11:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Payment for RDW-5421 — intermediary fees / bank chain question

Teresa — quick commercial note from my side. We generally ask strategic customers to select OUR where possible for high-value wires (> USD 25k equivalent) to avoid reconciliation overhead and unforecasted write-downs. For smaller invoices we can do beneficiary-net, but Redwood will either: (a) invoice the intermediary fees in a follow-up micro-invoice, or (b) absorb them if it's immaterial.

Given RDW-5421 is EUR 42,000 (above our pragmatic threshold), can you confirm your treasury can use OUR? If not, we'll accept SHA/BEN but we'll need the payment advice immediately after payment and we may bill back any intermediary bank fees.

If helpful, I'll loop in your treasury operations contact directly and share the OUR instruction template.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Teresa Moskowitz <teresa.moskowitz@astramed.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 9 Nov 2028 18:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Payment for RDW-5421 — intermediary fees / bank chain question

Teresa — Laura from Redwood finance here. Final point on the tax and reconciliation side: if AstraMed selects OUR, please ensure the payment advice explicitly states "OUR — payer to cover all intermediary/correspondent fees." That language helps our banks avoid routing the payment through optional intermediate nodes that may debit fees.

If AstraMed selects SHA/BEN and Redwood receives less than the invoice EUR equivalent, we'll record the shortfall as an intermediary bank expense. We'll then issue a short supporting debit note that shows: (a) original invoice, (b) gross payment amount per SWIFT, (c) actual net received, and (d) intermediary fees. That debit note will be a non-VAT financial adjustment in our system.

Please send the payment instruction (or confirm OUR) and a contact for your treasury so we can close the loop before your payment run.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Operations & Accounting
Redwood Inference
